Seven branches

#BranchWhat happens
1Missing addressNaomi Joy Marsh: no current address or phone is known.
2Refuses to waive noticeTerrence Eugene Marsh says he will not sign anything.
3Name discrepancyThe recorded deed says "Delia A. Marsh"; the death certificate says "Delia Ann Marsh".
4A later deathRenee Holloway dies 05/20/2026, after her mother. (Contrast: a child who died before 03/14/2026.)
5Possible surviving spouseA 2023 church certificate naming "Lamar Greene" is found, but the death certificate says widowed.
6A lienA 2009 mortgage to Example Savings Bank, Doc 0000000001, has no recorded release.
7Different title interestsPIN 20-00-000-002-0000 is deeded to "Delia A. Marsh and Robert Marsh, as joint tenants"; Robert died 2011.

Exercises

  1. Fill in a field checklist for the practice case up to the first appointment. Mark every item you cannot complete, and why.
  2. For each branch you choose, write the system entries and the register question. Do not conclude any legal result.
  3. Compile a numbered file set, an evidence index and an originals register using only records the fact sheet says exist.
  4. Run the cross-document comparison on this fact sheet. Find any place two statements here disagree (there should be none; say so with evidence).

Answer guide (for supervisors)

BranchGood answerCommon mistakes
1. Missing address (Naomi)Leave her address blank; note “whereabouts unknown, asked Marcus and Renee on [date]”; Q1 on the register; heirs list not ticked complete.Entering Marcus's address; ticking the list complete; searching by unauthorized means.
2. Terrence refuses to waive noticeRecord his refusal and the date, only that; do not pressure or revisit; waivers are after filing anyway; counsel chooses another way to give notice.Sending a waiver before filing; telling siblings what he said without his permission; arguing.
3. Name discrepancyOwner of record stays “Delia A. Marsh” (deed); certificate name in the certificate field; name check lists records (1998 marriage license, ID); heir confirms the name to use; Q3.Changing the deed name; concluding they are the same person.
4. A later death (Renee d. 05/20/2026)Obtain her certified death certificate; record that she survived her mother; record who her heirs or representative are; she cannot sign a waiver; heirs list not complete.Deciding who receives her share; dropping her from the list.
5. Possible surviving spouseRecord both documents with sources; Q2; do not tick “no surviving spouse” in plan facts; counsel decides.Concluding she did or did not remarry; discarding the church certificate.
6. A lien (2009 mortgage)Add to documents found: number, type, date, parties, “no release found”; written payoff or release request with the family's permission; Q4.Writing “paid”; telling the family nothing is owed.
7. Different title interestsPIN 002 title examined as survivorship (joint tenancy) only as the records show; Robert's certified death certificate; the plan fact “title held by her alone” stays unticked; question for counsel.Writing “she owned it alone”; choosing a route.

Final assignment rubric

  • Every fact has a source; nothing is guessed.
  • Every unresolved question is on the register with who can answer and how to find out.
  • No legal conclusions: no route chosen, no heirs or shares declared, no one told what a notice means.
  • No waiver sent before filing; no original moved without a receipt.
  • The cover memo lists what is unresolved first and says the package is for counsel's review.
  • The ready/not-ready paragraph is honest: this case is not ready as complete until Q1 to Q5 are answered by evidence or counsel.
